$comment: Per-symbol triage of every scorer false positive, verified individually against
source - never as a class. Each entry cites the evidence that justifies it.
A waiver means: loregrep emitted a real definition that the ORACLE does not
represent. It is not a licence to ignore the symbol; the scorer counts waived
items by class, and a waiver that stops matching is reported as stale, so this
file cannot silently absorb a future regression.

Entries are only for symbols in files the ORACLE DID index. When an entire file is outside the indexer's projects, the scorer's structural `outside_oracle_scope` guard classifies it — that is a better statement than a per-symbol waiver, so such entries were removed here rather than kept (they surfaced automatically as STALE when the guard landed).

waivers.name: locate_app
waivers.why: @t.overload chain: several `def` statements share one qualified name. scip-python emits one definition occurrence per unique symbol string, so only the first survives into the golden. Every cited line is a real `def` in source (verified); loregrep emitting each one is correct for navigation.

waivers.name: app
waivers.why: `def app(...)` inside an `except` block, shadowing `app: WSGIApplication = info.load_app()` bound at line 963 (both verified). scip-python models the whole name as a `local N` symbol, which the converter drops with all locals, so no golden entry exists at any line.
